region: Anti-Atlas, Siroua and Jbel Saghro, southern Morocco
title: Morocco — Granite, Saffron and the Saghro, Beyond the Classic Circuit
subtitle: Atlantic arches, the Anti-Atlas, the Siroua and four days with mules across the Jbel Saghro
summary: A 13-day route through southern Morocco that avoids Marrakech and Fès as the core and stays far from the Algerian border: Legzira, Tafraoute's granite, Taliouine and a mule-supported trek through the Jbel Saghro. Eligible on the advisories reviewed, with the French security map still to be confirmed.
introduction: Thirteen days that start on the Atlantic and end on foot in the volcanic Jbel Saghro. A rented SUV with two drivers goes from Agadir to the red arch at Legzira, then up into the pink granite of the Anti-Atlas at Tafraoute, where tents go up for two nights. Taliouine adds saffron and a day on the Siroua massif. The core is four days across the Saghro with a guide, cook and mules and three bivouacs. Marrakech is only the last night before the flight home. Mid-March follows Ramadan, with mild days and freezing nights.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is empty desert and wadis driven in a convoy of one; here the long days are walked with mules over a mountain range with no road, and the car is parked for four days. The landscape is volcanic and granite rather than sand, and the cultural contact is with Amazigh villages and shepherds, not Bedouin.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: The standard Morocco package runs Marrakech, Fès, the Merzouga dunes and Aït Ben Haddou. This route avoids all of those, uses family guesthouses and a village-hired trek crew, and its stages are mostly out of sight of coaches.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination in the portfolio combines an Atlantic sea arch, a pink-granite boulder field, a saffron town and a four-day mule trek across an untracked volcanic range inside one fortnight, at a total under the preferred budget.

duration.note: Day 1 and day 13 are flight days (Agadir in, Marrakech out). Day 12 is a long drive and transit night.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Starts after Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr (expected about 8 February to 9 March, moon-sighting dependent). Saghro days are mild and the Siroua and Tichka roads are usually open, though nights freeze. February would put the trek crews, drivers and village restaurants in Ramadan, although it has the almond blossom.

februarySuitability.summary: Almond blossom is at its best in the Ameln valley (festival in February) and skies are clear, but Ramadan (about 8 February onward) affects trek crews, daytime restaurants and opening hours, and Saghro nights drop well below freezing.

marchSuitability.summary: After Eid, services return to normal; Saghro days reach about 15–19 °C with nights between -3 and 4 °C. Blossom is over, snow can persist on the Siroua and Tichka in the first half of the month.

climate.regionNote: Planning ranges, not station-verified normals: Tafraoute and Taliouine at about 1,000–1,300 m, the Saghro plateau at about 1,500–2,200 m, Agadir on the coast. Mountain nights are the main unknown.

february.rainfall: Low to moderate; showers in the Anti-Atlas, snow possible above 2,000 m
february.notes: Saghro nights can fall to -5 °C at 2,000 m.

march.rainfall: Low to moderate; the last rains of winter
march.notes: Saghro plateau nights -3 to 4 °C; Agadir coast 12-14 °C at night.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Snow can lie on the Siroua and the Tizi n'Tichka (2,260 m) into March and close the pass for hours or days. Saghro passes are 1,800-2,300 m; the guide chooses lower alternatives if needed.
climate.seaConditions: Atlantic at Legzira is cold and rough; the beach walk depends on low tide, and swimming is not planned.
climate.airQuality: Good in the mountains; no seasonal haze noted.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Spring birds and flowers start in March; argan goats on the Anti-Atlas roads.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Daytime fasting affects trek crews, small-town restaurants, souks and shop hours; Eid al-Fitr is expected about 9–10 March, with holiday travel and busy transport.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Tafraoute almond blossom festival
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: Typically in February (date varies; a 2024 edition was on 23–24 February)
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Peak bloom is before the recommended window; a March trip sees leaf and late petals.

climate.ramadan2027: Ramadan is expected to begin about 8 February 2027 and end with Eid al-Fitr about 9 March (Morocco sets dates by moon sighting, so a one-day shift is possible). The recommended 13–25 March window follows it, so crews, drivers and restaurants are back to normal. A February trip would be possible with adjustments (self-catering, food from the guide, a rest-day cushion for fasting crews), but is judged less reliable.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Lunar New Year has no effect on Morocco.
climate.tourismDemand: Low in the Anti-Atlas and Saghro in March; busier on the Marrakech–Ouarzazate corridor.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Fare trackers show cheap Paris–Agadir return fares for March 2027 (about EUR 99-125 return on low-cost carriers), higher around Eid and Easter.

geography.summary: An Atlantic cliff coast, a granite basin, an oasis gorge, a volcanic massif and a dry volcanic range between the High Atlas and the Sahara.
geography.distinctive: The Saghro is a roadless volcanic range of dark plateaus and rock towers, reached on foot with mules; Tafraoute's boulder field is pink granite; both are far from the sand-dune circuit.

signatureExperiences.title: Four days across the Jbel Saghro with mules
signatureExperiences.description: Guide, cook and muleteers carry tents and food while you walk 5–6 h a day over plateaus and passes, camping at springs.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A roadless volcanic range with little tourist traffic, away from the dunes and kasbahs of the standard circuit.
signatureExperiences.location: Jbel Saghro, Nkob to Boumalne Dadès
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a local outfitter by message months ahead; fix route, price and what is included; hire guide, cook and mules together.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Group package EUR 600 split four ways, planning estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Legzira's sea arch at low tide
signatureExperiences.description: A walk on the beach beneath red cliffs and the arch, timed by the tide table.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: An Atlantic landscape that opens the trip before the mountains.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Self-guided; check the tide table the day before.

signatureExperiences.title: Two tent nights in the granite of Tafraoute
signatureExperiences.description: Pitch tents at a campsite, then walk through the Ameln valley and the Aït Mansour gorges.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Pink granite boulders, oasis gorges and terraced villages in one basin.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Self-drive; campsite in town; local guide for a Lekst walk if wanted.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Two campsite nights plus a share of a guide, estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Saffron town and a day on the Siroua
signatureExperiences.description: Visit a saffron cooperative at Taliouine, then walk on the Siroua with a local guide.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Saffron is grown only in this part of Morocco and the Siroua is a quiet volcanic massif.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a guide through the guesthouse; check snow before going up.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Guide share and cooperative visit, estimate.

travelStyle.summary: Self-drive between bases, with a four-day guided mule trek in the middle and two tent nights plus three bivouacs.

transport.summary: One rental SUV from Agadir, dropped at Marrakech; the Saghro is walked with an outfitter's mules and a 4x4 transfer.

modes.description: Two licence holders share about 1,450 km of mostly paved roads.
Transfer to the Nkob trailhead and baggage carried on mules.

transport.carRental: International and local firms operate at Agadir and Marrakech airports; one-way fees, minimum age (commonly 21–25), a licence held 1–2 years, and a card deposit apply. Confirm additional driver terms and that the vehicle can use unpaved tracks (most contracts forbid piste driving).

drivingRequirements.summary: Main roads are paved and good; mountain roads are winding and the Tizi n'Tichka can be icy. Night driving and overloaded trucks are hazards per FCDO. No piste driving is planned.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Conditional on licence country. FCDO guidance for UK drivers is a 1968 IDP and a green insurance card; French licences are normally accepted for short stays, but confirm with the rental firm.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences; both should be registered as drivers.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody rides a scooter, quad or motorcycle without the required licence. Use the car, the outfitter's 4x4, mules and taxis; quad rides are not planned (the FCDO warns on quad accidents).
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: One rental SUV, two registered drivers, daylight driving, no piste driving; the Saghro stage is guided and the car is parked.

accommodation.summary: Family guesthouses, a Tafraoute campsite for two nights and three bivouacs on the trek.

camping.summary: Two nights at a Tafraoute campsite and three bivouacs on the trek provided by the outfitter. Wild camping outside villages is generally tolerated with local permission, but not in protected areas; it is not relied on.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Four days of 4–6 h walking with 300–500 m of climbing at 1,500–2,200 m, sub-zero nights and rough footing; mules carry the load.

itinerary.summary: Thirteen days: Agadir, Tiznit, Legzira and Sidi Ifni, Tafraoute (two tent nights), Taliouine (two nights), Boumalne Dadès, a four-day Saghro trek, and Marrakech for the flight home. Two flexible days.

days.title: Fly to Agadir, collect the car, first night in Tiznit
activities: Fly Paris to Agadir Al Massira (direct flights operate; low-cost carriers may leave from Orly or Beauvais rather than CDG)
Collect the rental SUV at the airport, with both licence holders registered as drivers
Drive 90 km south to Tiznit, change money, buy a SIM card
Walk the walled old town and eat at a local grill
days.travelTime: ≈ 3 h 30 min flight; 1 h 15 min drive
days.accommodation: Guesthouse or riad in Tiznit, 2 twin rooms
days.practical: Collect the car in daylight; fill the tank before leaving Tiznit.

days.title: Legzira's sea arch and Sidi Ifni
activities: Drive the coast road to Legzira beach (about 65 km) and time the walk for low tide
Walk the red cliffs and the sea arch, 2 h round trip
Continue to Sidi Ifni, a former Spanish enclave with an Art Deco centre
Fish lunch at the port and evening on the cliff-top promenade
days.accommodation: Guesthouse in Sidi Ifni, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Sidi Ifni's Spanish-era Art Deco buildings
days.geographicalHighlight: Red sandstone cliffs and Atlantic sea arch
days.practical: Check the tide table: the beach is passable around low tide only. Stay off the south-east of Guelmim province (residual mines per France Diplomatie) and do not drive to Plage Blanche.

days.title: Over to the pink granite of the Anti-Atlas
activities: Drive back through Tiznit and up into the Anti-Atlas to Tafraoute (about 185 km)
Walk among the painted boulders and Napoleon's Hat before dusk
Pitch tents at a campsite in Tafraoute (tent night 1)
Dinner of tagine and argan-oil bread in town
days.culturalHighlight: Amazigh Chleuh villages of the Tafraoute basin
days.geographicalHighlight: Pink granite boulder field around Tafraoute
days.practical: The road climbs to about 1,000 m; nights in March are 5-8 °C, so bring sleeping bags rated to 0 °C. A gîte is the fallback in rain.

days.title: Ameln valley, Aït Mansour gorges and Jbel Lekst
activities: Drive into the Ameln valley and walk between almond, argan and palm terraces and villages
Short drive southwest to the Aït Mansour gorges and its palm oasis
Walk a 2-3 h section of the lower slopes of Jbel Lekst with a local guide
Second tent night; buy bread, olives and almonds at the Tafraoute souk if it is open
days.culturalHighlight: Fortified granaries and terraced villages of the Ameln valley
days.geographicalHighlight: Granite ridge of Jbel Lekst, oasis gorge
days.practical: Almond blossom is mainly a February event; in mid-March the terraces are green and bare of petals. Check road conditions in the gorge after rain.

days.title: North to the saffron town below the Siroua
activities: Drive about 250 km via Aït Baha and the N10 to Taliouine (route to be confirmed on the day)
Stop at a roadside market or argan cooperative
Visit the old Taliouine kasbah and a saffron cooperative
Evening in a family guesthouse
days.culturalHighlight: Taliouine kasbah and the saffron trade
days.geographicalHighlight: Edge of the Jbel Siroua massif
days.practical: A long day: swap driving between the two licence holders every 90 min. Fuel up at Taroudant.

days.title: Jbel Siroua day walk (weather and rest day)
activities: Walk a day route on the Siroua massif with a local guide, 4-6 h, from villages above Taliouine
Alternative: Tislit gorges or the saffron fields near town
Use the day as a buffer if snow, rain or fatigue move the plan
Second night in the same guesthouse
days.transport: Walk; rental car for the trailhead
days.culturalHighlight: Aït Siroua villages with Amazigh farming
days.geographicalHighlight: Volcanic Siroua massif; snow possible on upper slopes
days.practical: Do not attempt the summit in snow without a guide and winter gear; the lower valley walks are the plan.

days.title: Across the south to the foot of the Saghro
activities: Drive about 340 km via Ouarzazate and Kelaat M'Gouna to Boumalne Dadès
Lunch in Ouarzazate, bypassing the film-set and tour-bus stops
Meet the trek outfitter at the guesthouse and fix the route, gear and cash for the crew
Early night before the trek
days.accommodation: Guesthouse in Boumalne Dadès, 2 twin rooms
days.practical: The longest drive of the trip; two drivers share. The car stays parked at the guesthouse during the trek.

days.title: Saghro trek, day 1: transfer to the trailhead and first walk
activities: Outfitter 4x4 takes the group, guide, cook and mules to the Nkob side (about 2 h 30 min)
Walk 3–4 h from the trailhead to the first bivouac with the mule team
Camp near a spring on the plateau
Dinner cooked by the crew in a shared tent
days.culturalHighlight: Aït Atta pastoral life on the plateau
days.geographicalHighlight: Dark volcanic ridges and dry plateaus of the Jbel Saghro
days.practical: Sleeping bags to -5 °C are needed; March nights can freeze at 1,500–2,000 m. The outfitter provides tents, mats, food and drinking water.

days.title: Saghro trek, day 2: plateaus and passes
activities: Walk 5–6 h across the plateau and over a pass with 300–500 m of climbing
Lunch in the open; mules carry tents and bags
Pass nomad camps or villages and buy bread with the guide
Bivouac near a village or well
days.culturalHighlight: Meetings with Aït Atta shepherds, arranged by the guide
days.practical: The route is not waymarked: do not walk it without the guide. Keep two spare days of food in the plan.

days.title: Saghro trek, day 3: the high section
activities: Walk 5–6 h across the high central section, with views over the Drâa and Dadès sides
Visit a village and, if invited, take tea in a house
Bivouac at a spring
Stargazing from camp, with almost no light pollution
days.culturalHighlight: Village visit arranged through the guide
days.practical: If snow or rain blocks the pass, the guide takes a lower alternative; this is the day most affected by weather.

days.title: Saghro trek, day 4: down to the Dadès valley
activities: Walk 4–5 h downhill and along dry valleys to the road at the Dadès side
Say goodbye to the crew and tip them according to the outfitter's guide
Hot showers and a good meal at the guesthouse
Rest and repack
days.accommodation: Guesthouse in Boumalne Dadès, 2 twin rooms
days.practical: The finish point is agreed with the outfitter before departure; if weather delays the trek, day 12 absorbs the delay.

days.title: Back over the High Atlas to Marrakech
activities: Drive about 340 km via Ouarzazate and the Tizi n'Tichka pass to Marrakech
Stop at the pass viewpoints, checking for snow or ice before the climb
Return the rental car at Marrakech airport or in the city (one-way fee applies)
Evening in Marrakech: a transit night, not a sightseeing day
days.practical: The Tizi n'Tichka can close for snow in winter; the alternative is to leave earlier and check conditions with the guesthouse.

days.title: Fly home
activities: Taxi to Marrakech Menara airport
Fly Marrakech to Paris
Arrive in the afternoon or evening
days.practical: Direct flights are normal on this route; check the schedule and baggage terms.

security.summary: The route lies in Souss-Massa, Guelmim-Oued Noun, Drâa-Tafilalet and Marrakech-Safi, about 200 km or more from the closed Algerian border and far from Western Sahara and the Mauritanian border. FCDO names no area against travel on the route, and Netherlands Worldwide is yellow except for the Algerian and Mauritanian border zones. France's interactive map could not be read directly, and the US State Department page could not be fetched, so the status rests on the reviewed sources and must be confirmed.
security.assessedRoute: Agadir, Tiznit, Legzira, Sidi Ifni, Tafraoute, Taliouine, Boumalne Dadès, Nkob and the Jbel Saghro, Tizi n'Tichka, Marrakech. Explicitly excluded: M'hamid, Erg Chigaga, Tata, Akka, Figuig, the Algerian border area, Plage Blanche and the south-east of Guelmim province (residual mines), the Mauritanian border and Western Sahara.

advisories.level: Country page last updated 10 September 2026; the PDF fiche (April 2026) classes the Mauritanian border as formally advised against and notes residual mines in the south-east of Guelmim province; interactive zones not read
advisories.regionsAffected: Mauritanian border; mined zone of south-east Guelmim
advisories.routeImpact: The route does not enter either area; the Algerian border zone could not be confirmed from France's own pages.

advisories.level: Regional-risks page names only the closed Algerian border and Western Sahara as disputed territory; no area against all or all-but-essential travel is named for the route
advisories.routeImpact: No route area affected; terrorism attacks 'likely' country-wide, road accidents frequent.

advisories.level: Yellow for the rest of Morocco; orange for the Algerian border area; red for the Mauritanian border area of Western Sahara
advisories.routeImpact: Route stays clear of orange and red zones; M'hamid and Erg Chigaga are omitted for this reason.

conflictRisk.note: Land borders with Algeria are closed and militarised; the route stays far from them.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO says attacks are likely to be attempted at tourist sites, transport hubs and crowded places; the route avoids major crowds, but airports and Marrakech are generic targets.

kidnappingRisk.note: No kidnapping warning for the route was found in the pages read.

regionalRestrictions: Do not approach the Algerian border zone (M'hamid, Erg Chigaga, Figuig, Tata-Akka south) or the Mauritanian border.
Avoid Plage Blanche and the south-east of Guelmim province (residual mines per France Diplomatie).
Do not attempt to cross land borders; Western Sahara is not part of the route.
ordinaryRisks: Road accidents on mountain roads and at night
Earthquakes (the 2023 High Atlas quake killed almost 3,000 people)
Petty crime and pestering by false guides in tourist towns
Snow, ice and cold at altitude; flash floods in gorges after rain
Quad and adventure providers not meeting UK safety standards
security.medicalAccess: Hospitals in Agadir and Marrakech; clinics in towns; the Saghro is hours from care, so a guide with a satellite or radio plan and an evacuation clause are needed.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Check cover for trekking up to 2,500 m with a guide, evacuation by helicopter or vehicle, and that insurance is valid for the advised areas.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; read France's interactive security map and the US State Department page directly; downgrade to conditional or excluded if the Algerian or Mauritanian border zones widen, if any route province becomes orange, or if Tichka or Saghro access is restricted.

practicalRequirements.visa: Visa-free for French citizens for short stays; other nationalities must check Morocco's entry rules. Not assumed.
practicalRequirements.entry: Passport and onward ticket; customs and drug laws are strict.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: Commonly at least six months for many nationalities; verify for each passport.
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with trekking and evacuation cover.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: 4G in towns; none or weak on the Saghro trek, with the guide carrying a phone.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards in Agadir and Marrakech; cash dirhams for guesthouses, crew and villages; ATMs in Tafraoute and Boumalne.
practicalRequirements.medical: Carry personal medicines; tap water not recommended.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Fill up at Tiznit, Taroudant and Boumalne Dadès; none on the trek.
